newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli unions in nationwide strike.
newsitem.headline: Israeli unions in nationwide strike.

text.p: Israeli unions launched a nationwide wildcat strike on Thursday to support communications workers battling privatisation moves.

Tel Aviv's Ben-Gurion international airport was particularly hit hard by the open-ended stoppage by workers in state-owned companies and institutions. Takeoffs were suspended but planes were allowed to land, although baggage was not being unloaded.
"The Histadrut (labour federation) is dragging the economy towards chaos," Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's spokesman said in a statement after the strike began at 0400 GMT.

The Histadrut said some 60,000 workers at the Israel Airports Authority, Israel Electric Company, Israeli Military Industries, Israel Aircraft Industries, the Postal Authority, the railroads and other state-owned institutions like El Al Israel Airlines were taking part.
"The impact is very bad, especially on the economy of the state of Israel," Finance Minister Yaacov Neeman told reporters.

The stoppage was declared hours after the government issued an order to force hundreds of Bezeq Israel Telecom employees to restore essential telephone services disrupted in a week-long strike by workers at the country's main telecoms provider.

Union leaders at Bezeq called the move "totalitarian" and said a crisis continued over government plans to privatise more of the state-owned company through the $250 million sale of 12.5 percent of its stock to Merrill Lynch.

Union leaders said the Merrill Lynch deal violated government promises to involve Bezeq workers in all aspects of the company's privatisation and called for the sale to be cancelled or to use its revenues to fund early pension programmes.

"(Thursday's) strike is unnecessary and will not affect the government's intention of opening the economy to competition in various fields while protecting workers' rights," Netanyahu's spokesman said.
